West Pakistan Municipal Committees (Recovery Of Taxes) Rules 1962
West Pakistan Municipal Committees (Recovery Of Taxes) Rules 1962
[Gazette of West
Pakistan,
Extraordinary, 7th April 1962]
No. S. O. I. (LG)-25-A-Misc/62. In exercise of the powers conferred
by sections 38, 41 and 121 of the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960
(Ordinance X of 1960), read with items 23 and 25 of the Fourth Schedule
thereto, the Governor of West Pakistan is pleased to make the following rules,
namely:
1. Short
title and commencement. (1) These rules may be called the West Pakistan Municipal
Committees (Recovery of Taxes) Rules, 1962.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
(3) For the purposes of section
38 (3) of the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960, these shall apply to
all Municipal Committees in West Pakistan.
2. Definitions. In these rules, unless, the context otherwise requires, the following expression shall have the meanings
hereby respectively assigned to them, that is to say
(a) "Chairman" means
the Chairman of the Municipal Committee;
(b) "costs of recovery" includes
the .charges specified in these rules;
(c) "defaulter"
means any person from whom any amount is recoverable under these rules and
which has remained unpaid after the presentation of a bill to him under rule
30;
(d) "Form" means a form
appended to these rules;
(e) "Ordinance" means the Municipal Administration
Ordinance, 1960 (X of 1960); and
(f) "Taxation Officer" means the Officer Incharge of the
Taxation Department of the Municipal Committee and any other officer declared
by the Municipal Committee to be Taxation Officer for the purposes of these
rules.
3. Presentation of bills
for taxes. (1) When any amount on account of a tax shall have become due, the Taxation Officer
shall, with the least practicable delay, cause to be presented to the
person liable for the payment thereof a bill for the sum claimed as due.
(2) Every such bill shall specify--
(a) the
period for which, and the property, occupation or thing in respect of which the
sum is claimed;
(b) the
liability to be incurred in the event of default; and
(c) the
time within which, and the authority to whom an appeal may be preferred against
such claim.
4. Notice
of demand. (1) If the sum for which any bill has been presented under rule
3 is not paid within fifteen days from the presentation thereof, the Taxation
Officer may cause to be served upon the defaulter a notice of demand in Form I.
(2) For every notice of demand, a
charge of one rupee shall be levied to cover the cost of the notice and its
service, and such charge shall be included in the tax to be recovered from the
defaulter
5. Issue
of warrants. (1) If the defaulter does not within fifteen days of
the service of the notice of demand
(a) pay
the sum demanded in the notice of the demand; or
(b) show
cause to the satisfaction of the Chairman why he should not pay the same; or
(c) prefer
an appeal in accordance with the provisions of the West Pakistan Municipal
Committees (Appeals) Rules, 1960;
the
Chairman may direct that the tax with all costs of recovery shall be recovered
under a warrant by distress and sale of the movable property belonging to the
defaulter, or by attachment and sale of the immovable property belonging to
him.
(2) The warrant issued under
sub-rule (1) shall be in Form II, and shall be signed by the Chairman.
(3) Where the property is within
the municipality, the warrant shall be addressed to the Taxation Officer, and
where the property is outside the municipality, to the Collector of the
district concerned:
Provided that the officer to whom
the warrant is addressed may endorse such warrant to a subordinate officer.
(4) For every warrant issued
under this rule, a sum of rupees five shall be charged, and this amount shall
be included in the cost of recovery.
